title: 7/7 things quietly wrecking your mornings
format: Notes listicle on white (title says 7, deck has 6), app as a confession inside point 3 with its morning step screen in a phone
why: Second take on amayareading's 182K-like / 58K-save listicle, morning angle: white page, lowercase Inter, 'N/N' title over one striking cutout image with a small right-aligned aside, then one habit per slide with a partly underlined heading, short paragraphs on the mechanism, one candid photo beside the text, and the app's morning screen in a phone on slide 4 inside the 'i struggled with this until…' paragraph. Ends on content, no closer, like the ref.
caption: which one got you this morning? #morningroutine #screentime #snooze #sleep
sound: slow moody alt rock, low volume (the ref uses deftones – shmeswon)
check: slide 4: 'what finally fixed it: my apps now stay asleep…' must be true for you (it's your own app; the 'Your brand' disclosure covers that)
slide 4: the phone shows the real step-count Home render (02-steps-clean); 200 steps is the app's real default
slide 3: the alarm list is a drawn iOS-style screenshot (not our app); slides 3 and 5 lines are common sleep advice, kept general
AI-made photos (slides 1, 2, 3, 5, 6; no faces): turn on TikTok's AI-generated label
promo: turn on TikTok's "Your brand" disclosure
slide 1: the two sleep charts are drawn illustrations in the style of a sleep tracker, not anyone's real data

slides.heading: checking your phone _before you sit up_
slides.top: eyes half open, thumb already on the screen: _group chats, emails_, someone's holiday
slides.text:
your brain starts the day _reacting_ instead of waking up

by the time your feet touch the floor you're _already behind_
slides.bottom: sit up first, then pick up the phone

slides.heading: the _snooze_ button
slides.top: nine more minutes, _four times in a row_
slides.text:
each snooze starts a sleep _you never finish_

so you get up groggier than at the _first alarm_
slides.bottom: one alarm you get up for beats five you argue with

slides.heading: your apps _waking up before you_
slides.text:
at 7am the feed is wide awake and _you aren't_

so the first thing you do is whatever is _closest to your hand_

what finally fixed it: my apps now _stay asleep until i've walked 200 steps_

slides.heading: staying _in the dark_
slides.top: curtains shut, scrolling under the duvet _until 8:40_
slides.text:
your body is waiting for _light_ to start the day

no light, so the morning _never really starts_
slides.bottom: open the curtains before you open the apps

slides.heading: a night that _ended at 2am_
slides.text:
most bad mornings were decided _the night before_

and no coffee fixes _five hours of sleep_
slides.bottom: fix the night first, then worry about the morning routine
